Sub: Notice of 31st Annual General Meeting and Annual Report for FY 2025-26  
 
Dear Sir/ Ma’am, 
 
This is further to our communication dated July 15, 2026 wherein the Company informed about its 31st Annual 
General Meeting (‘AGM’).  
 
Please note that the AGM will be held on Tuesday, August 11, 2026 at 11:30 A.M. (IST) through Video 
Conferencing (‘VC’) in accordance with relevant circulars issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (‘Circulars’). 
 
In terms of the provisions of applicable laws and circulars, the Notice of AGM (‘Notice’) and Annual Report for FY 
2025-26 (‘Annual Report’), are being sent through email only, to all those members whose names are appearing 
in the Register of Members/ List of Beneficial Owners received from the depositories as on Friday, July 10, 2026 
and whose email addresses are registered with the Company/ Depository Participants/ Depositories/ Registrar & 
Share Transfer Agent of the Company. 
 
The Notice, inter-alia, covers the detailed instructions for e-voting, attendance at the AGM through VC and 
registration of email addresses by the Members. Further, a physical communication (enclosed herewith) is also 
being sent by the Company to all those Members, whose email addresses are not registered/ updated in records, 
which contains the exact link and a QR code of the Company’s website to access the Notice, Annual Report and 
other relevant documents.  
 
In compliance with the applicable laws, the Company is providing the facility of remote e-voting and e-voting at 
the AGM to its Members in respect of all the resolutions set forth in the Notice. The cut-off date for the purpose of 
reckoning the voting rights of Members for this AGM is Tuesday, August 04, 2026 (‘Cut-off date’). Accordingly, 
all eligible members as on Cut-off date shall be entitled for e-voting. The remote e-voting shall commence from 
9.00 a.m. (IST) on Friday, August 07, 2026 and shall remain open till 5.00 p.m. (IST) on Monday, August 
10, 2026. 
 
The Notice and Annual Report are enclosed herewith and are also available on the Company’s website at 
https://www.bhartihexacom.in/results-annual-results.html.  
 
The above intimation is being made under Regulations 30, 34 and 44 and other applicable provisions of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. 
 
Kindly take the above on record. 
 
Thanking you, 
Sincerely Yours, 
 
For Bharti Hexacom Limited     
 
 
 
Amit Chaturvedi 
Company Secretary and Compliance Officer

At Bharti Hexacom, customer 
obsession shapes every 
strategic decision we 
make. Every investment we 
undertake, every capability 
we strengthen and every 
innovation we pursue is 
anchored in a clear purpose: 
to simplify lives and 
deliver secure and reliable 
connectivity. As digital 
adoption accelerates across 
our markets, we remain 
focused on understanding 
evolving expectations, 
expanding access and creating 
lasting value for the customers 
and communities we serve.
During the year, we continued to expand the 
digital foundations of Rajasthan and the North-
East through sustained investments in 5G 
footprint expansion, network densification and 
enhanced rural coverage. We also extended 
the reach of high-speed broadband through 
Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), enabling more 
households to participate in an increasingly 
connected world.
Our convergence strategy reached a new 
milestone with the launch of IPTV, bringing 
together mobility, broadband and entertainment 
within a seamless digital ecosystem. This 
proposition is strengthening our engagement 
with customers by enhancing convenience 
and enriching everyday experiences across the 
connected home.
At the same time, our AI-led transformation 
gained significant momentum. By embedding 
AI across networks, operations and customer 
journeys, we are improving agility, elevating 
customer experiences and building a stronger 
competitive advantage.
The opportunities ahead remain significant. 
Supported by resilient infrastructure, 
differentiated capabilities and a deep 
understanding of the markets we serve, we are 
well positioned to accelerate digital inclusion, 
unlock new avenues of growth and create 
sustainable value.

A B O U T B H A R T I H E X A C O M
Powering Digital Lives 
Beyond Connectivity 
Bharti Hexacom, a subsidiary 
of Bharti Airtel Limited, serves 
over 29 million customers across 
Rajasthan and the North-East with a 
comprehensive suite of connectivity 
and digital solutions. Our portfolio 
includes mobility, homes, business 
broadband, fixed-line services and 
IPTV along with a growing range 
of digital offerings from the Airtel 
ecosystem.
Our investments are focused on expanding 
our 5G footprint, deepening rural 
connectivity and modernising network 
capabilities, supported by a robust 
spectrum portfolio. These investments are 
accelerating digital inclusion and enabling 
the next wave of innovation.
Consistent ARPU growth, a disciplined 
focus on customer quality and sustained 
gains in revenue market share reflect the 
strength of our strategy. As digital adoption 
accelerates across our markets, we remain 
well positioned to drive sustainable growth 
and help shape the digital future of the 
markets we serve.

From Connectivity to 
Convergence
We continued 
to expand our 
addressable market 
by strengthening 
network leadership, 
accelerating 
digital adoption 
and expanding 
our portfolio of 
connectivity and 
digital services. 
By connecting more 
customers and 
expanding access 
to homes, we are 
delivering seamless 
experiences to 
create a platform 
for sustainable 
growth.
Our mobility business maintained strong 
momentum, supported by an improving 
customer mix, rising smartphone 
penetration and differentiated offerings 
that enhanced customer value. Continued 
adoption of 5G services, coupled with 
sustained rural expansion, further 
strengthened our market position.
Home Broadband is playing a pivotal role in 
expanding our presence across high value 
homes. Continued expansion of our Fiber-to-
the-Home (FTTH) and Fixed Wireless Access 
(FWA) footprint extended access to high-
speed broadband, resulting in highest-ever 
net customer additions during FY2025-26. 
FWA is accelerating broadband penetration 
in markets with relatively weaker fiber 
presence.
Our convergence strategy strengthens 
customer relationships by bringing together 
mobility, broadband, Digital TV and digital 
services within a unified ecosystem. A 
compelling content portfolio reinforces 
this proposition, offering access to 29 OTT 
platforms and 697 TV channels through 
strong regional and global partnerships. The 
launch of IPTV marked another important 
milestone in enriching the home experience 
through integrated entertainment and 
simplified customer journeys. Together, 
these initiatives are increasing our share 
among high-value homes, enhancing 
customer lifetime value and reinforcing the 
strength of our integrated proposition.

C H A I R M A N ’ S M E S S A G E 
Leading with 
Customers at the Core
FY 2025-26 has been a 
rewarding year for your 
Company, reaffirming 
our long-held conviction 
that results follow 
naturally when we build 
the best networks, 
listen to our customers, 
and relentlessly execute 
our strategy. 
Over the last five years, 
your Company invested H98 
billion towards building its 
digital network. 
Central to these core tenets has been 
our endeavour to extend a reliable and 
robust network, built on the foundation of 
uncompromising safety for all our customers. 
Your Company has strengthened its network 
capabilities with a focus on reliability and 
resilience, whether that be through scaling 
our network footprint or by leveraging 
AI-powered anti-spam solution. We have 
continually raised the bar for what a telecom 
Company can do. These efforts continue to 
define our journey as a trusted provider of 
digital connectivity.
As data consumption accelerates and 
digital services become increasingly 
integral to economic activity, your 
Company’s role has expanded beyond 
connecting the people of Rajasthan 
and the North-East to the world. Today, 
we are enabling digital inclusion, 
strengthening economic participation 
and helping build a safer and an even 
more digitally empowered future for the 
communities we serve.
Connecting India’s growth frontiers
In the past year, the Indian economy 
demonstrated remarkable resilience 
and remains among the fastest-growing 
major economies globally. Despite global 
headwinds arising from tariff-related 
disruptions, trade policy uncertainty 
and geopolitical tensions in West Asia, 
India’s growth has been anchored 
in robust domestic consumption. A 
reform-oriented policy environment has 
reinforced India’s sustainable growth 
trajectory. At the same time, rapid 
improvements in connectivity, coupled 
with sustained enhancements in the 
country’s digital public infrastructure, 
have emerged as critical pillars of a 
more connected and digitally-enabled 
economy. The regulatory environment 
remains constructive, supporting 
long-term investments and innovation. 
Our regulator, the Telecom Regulatory 
Authority of India (TRAI) has continued 
to provide a stable and enabling policy 
framework while remaining consistently 
responsive to industry concerns.
The Rajasthan and North-East circles, 
where your Company operates, continue 
to deliver strong growth supported 
by meaningful headroom for mobile 
penetration and a significant growth 
opportunity in home broadband. In both 
regions, Government investment in 
digital infrastructure and connectivity is 
creating the necessary foundation for 
long-term economic growth. Rajasthan’s 
Vision 2047 development ambitions 
are accelerating digital adoption and 
Dear Shareholders,
generating demand for high-quality 
connectivity. In the North-East, the 
region’s role as India’s gateway to 
ASEAN under the Government’s Act 
East Policy makes high-speed, reliable 
digital infrastructure, a strategic asset.
This policy highlights the growing 
importance of high-speed and reliable 
digital infrastructure as a strategic 
asset. Together, these developments are 
strengthening the role of connectivity 
as a critical enabler of economic 
participation and sustainable growth.
These progressive developments, 
alongside a growing tourism industry, 
have created a strong foundation for 
sustained growth in the telecom sector. 
As economic activity expands and 
digital adoption accelerates across both 
regions, your Company is well positioned 
to support this next phase of growth 
through reliable connectivity, digital 
services and investment in network 
infrastructure.
Building a digital network
Bharti Hexacom invested decisively 
during the year to strengthen the digital 
infrastructure underpinning growth 
across Rajasthan and the North-East. 
Over the last five years, your Company 
invested H98 billion towards building its 
digital network. During FY 2025-26, we 
deployed 245 towers and 3,657 base 
stations to strengthen our footprint and 
improve coverage quality, alongside 
investments in 5G networks. Through our 
Rural Acceleration Programme, we rolled 
out nearly 2,900 sites over the last three 
years, thereby unlocking access to digital 
commerce and payments for previously 
underserved communities.

Your Company also accelerated the 
roll-out of Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), 
further expanding our 5G-powered 
home broadband offering at scale. With 
domestic broadband penetration still at 
a nascent stage across the circles we 
operate, FWA is enabling us to address 
a significant untapped opportunity while 
expanding access to reliable, high-speed 
connectivity.
Further, I am delighted to share that 
our 5G network is now fully standalone 
(SA) ready. This strategic milestone 
distinguishes the company as the 
first domestic operator to provide a 
dual-mode 5G network, concurrently 
supporting both Standalone (SA) and 
Non-Standalone (NSA) configurations 
providing a future-ready foundation 
for advanced network slicing and low 
latency applications. Our FWA offering 
already operates on a SA network aimed 
to deliver brilliant customer experience.
Artificial Intelligence is becoming an 
increasingly important capability across 
our operations, from simplifying our 
network operations to intelligent capacity 
planning, smart site deployment, 
energy optimisation and predictive field 
engineering support. AI is helping us 
simplify complexity, improve efficiency 
and enhance the quality of service 
delivered to our customers.
Performance rooted in customer-
centricity
During FY 2025-26, your Company 
delivered strong performance driven by 
sustained investments, sharp execution 
and operational excellence. Bharti 
Hexacom fortified its leadership position 
in the North-East and sustained positive 
momentum in Rajasthan, resulting in 
our life-time high revenue market share 
across the two circles. This reflects the 
consistent progress we have made over 
the past five years, during which our 
revenue market share improved by 925 
basis points to reach 46%.
I am pleased to share that mobile 
customer base expanded to 28.8 million, 
with ~645K net additions during the 
year. In addition, smartphone data 
customers grew to 22.7 million and now 
account for 79% of our mobile base. Our 
Wi-Fi customer base witnessed robust 
net additions of ~395K supported by a 
deeper fiber footprint, the expansion of 
FWA to newer pin codes and launch  
of IPTV.
The strong growth in our customer 
base and continued focus on portfolio 
premiumisation translated into robust 
financial performance. Revenues 
increased by 9.4% to H93,538 million in 
FY 2025-26, driven by healthy customer 
additions across segments and improved 
quality of acquisitions. Mobile ARPU 
increased by 4.5% to H252, accompanied 
by a 28% increase in data consumption. 
EBITDAaL stood at H44,563 million 
registering a growth of 17.9%. EBITDAaL 
margins improved by 343 basis points 
to 47.6%. Capex for the year stood 
at H15,210 million, reflecting strong 
operational discipline and calibrated 
spending. These strategic investments 
resulted in an all-time high operating 
free cash flow of H29,353 million while 
maintaining a prudent net debt to 
EBITDAaL of 0.5 times. 
Backed by your Company’s consistent 
performance and strong cash 
generation, the Board recommended a 
dividend of H18 per share, representing 
an 80% year-on-year increase, in line with 
its philosophy of progressively enhancing 
returns to shareholders.
Customer obsession anchored in 
safety and experience
At Bharti Hexacom, our customers 
are at the centre of everything we do. 
Every investment we make, whether in 
strengthening our network, leveraging 
digital capabilities from our parent 
Bharti Airtel or enhancing the value and 
convenience of our offerings, is guided by 
a singular objective: delivering customer 
delight. 
This approach is deeply rooted in our 
culture, reinforced by a strong sense of 
ownership and entrepreneurial agility. It 
is reflected in our focus on differentiated 
offerings, simplified customer journeys 
across channels and our digital-first 
engagement. Whether through 
compelling content partnerships, 
customer-centric international roaming 
plans or frictionless service experiences, 
we remain committed to creating 
greater value for our customers at every 
touchpoint.
During the year, your Company also 
launched IPTV services to accelerate 
its convergence play. Our IPTV offering 
blends linear TV channels with 
on-demand content from leading 
streaming apps backed by our 
high-speed Wi-Fi network. We are 
seeing strong customer adoption and 
improving bundle attach rates, validating 
the growing demand for integrated 
connectivity and entertainment offerings.
Our AI powered anti-spam solution, 
launched in September 2024, has 
been a game changer, having provided 
substantial relief from unwanted 
communications to our customers. 
During the year, your Company 
strengthened this solution with 
new features, including detection 
and blocking of malicious websites, 
prevention of One Time Password related 
bank frauds and spam alerts across 
multiple vernacular languages, ensuring 
ubiquitous access to such protection 
across our customer base. 
Since its launch, this tool has flagged over 
5.1 billion spam calls, identified more than 
350 million spam messages and blocked 
over 1.1 million fraudulent links. 
Connected to a better future
The opportunity before us is significant. 
As data consumption rises, digital 
adoption deepens and technologies such 
as 5G and AI unlock new possibilities, the 
role of digital infrastructure will become 
even more critical. Bharti Hexacom will 
invest decisively in strengthening its 
networks and capabilities, maintaining a 
disciplined focus on execution and long-
term value creation.
As a conscious corporate citizen, 
Environmental, Social and Governance 
principles are integral to how your Company 
operates and scales its business. We are 
working to green our network and reduce 
emissions through diesel use optimisation 
and the deployment of solar access across 
our sites. 
In addition, your Company contributes 
to broader social development through 
initiatives that advance digital inclusion and 
expand access to quality education. Through 
the work of Bharti Airtel Foundation, we 
remain committed to creating meaningful 
and lasting impact within the communities 
we serve. Equally important are our 
employees, whose safety and well-being are 
paramount to us. We are investing in future-
ready skilling and digitally-enabled safety 
practices to empower our people and foster 
a culture of excellence.
As Rajasthan and the North-East advance 
in their journey of digital transformation, 
Bharti Hexacom is well-positioned to play 
a critical role in enabling the next phase of 
growth and sustained innovation. Backed 
by strong fundamentals, disciplined capital 
allocation and a clear long-term vision, your 
Company is focused on creating enduring 
value for customers, communities and 
shareholders alike.
I thank our Board for their wise counsel, our 
management team and employees for their 
relentless commitment, and our customers, 
partners, suppliers, distributors and valued 
shareholders for the trust they continue to 
place in us. 
JS Deepak
Chairman

Built on trust, 
guided by principle

Our approach to corporate governance
Governance practices at Bharti Hexacom are anchored in 
robust systems and structures, policies and processes and 
effective internal controls. Our robust Board and Committee 
framework sets the tone, ensuring stringent oversight of 
compliance matters alongside aligning the organisation with 
the evolving regulations in the telecom industry.
A robust Code of Conduct shapes our policies and processes 
and guides business decisions. It applies to the entire 
organisation, irrespective of hierarchy, promoting integrity 
and a culture of compliance and responsible practices. 
We also have a dedicated Code of Conduct for business 
associates, which guides their actions and helps ensure high 
ethical standards and ESG practices across the supply chain.
In FY 2025-26, there were no reported breaches of the Code 
or unethical practices.
Governance framework
We follow a top-down approach to corporate governance, 
with the Board and its Committees providing strategic 
oversight at the top level. The Senior Management 
undertakes executive responsibilities, ensuring compliance 
across financial, operational, and ESG aspects. The Company 
Secretary is responsible for smooth Board functioning, 
legal compliance and transparent and timely disclosures 
to the stakeholder community. Compliance is reinforced 
through regular audits by Independent auditors and internal 
assurance partners, assuring stakeholders of the integrity of 
our operations. For all material decisions, approval is sought 
from shareholders as per regulatory requirements.
Sustainability governance
Our sustainability governance framework is underpinned by 
strong Board oversight and robust ethical practices, driving 
accountability, transparency, and responsible business 
conduct. ESG regime of Bharti Hexacom Limited operates 
under group-wide regime of Bharti Airtel Limited (Holding 
Company). 
Board composition
Our Board comprises a diverse mix of Directors across 
experiences, areas of expertise, independence and gender, 
in full compliance with the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI 
Listing Regulations. 40% (4 members) of our Board are 
Non-Executive Directors (including the Chairman) and 60% 
(6 members) are Independent Directors. This deliberate 
mix of experience and independence ensures balanced 
oversight, strategic continuity and objectivity in decisions.
Board composition is periodically reviewed to ensure 
the right mix of skills and diversity as per the evolving 
regulatory needs and business priorities. Our Board does 
not have permanent seats, and all appointments, including 
rotational reappointments, are approved by shareholders. 
All Directors comply with SEBI norms on Committee 
memberships, with none chairing more than five or serving 
on more than ten committees across companies.

structured framework. In FY 2025-26, it evaluated 
the Board on parameters including their strategic 
contribution to long-term objectives, leadership 
qualities, oversight responsibilities, and preparedness.

to operate effectively, demonstrating progress in 
priorities, top-down flow of information and active 
participation in advancing objectives through 
structured meetings and effective decisions. It confirms 
the diverse and complementary expertise of our Board,

compliance, risk management, safe working conditions,

employees, partners, vendors, and all work-related 
environments, including off-site and virtual interactions.

Overview
The telecom sector plays an integral role in India’s digital 
transformation by enabling economic growth, accelerating 
innovation, and improving access to services for enterprises 
and individuals alike. Sustained investments by telecom 
operators in advanced technologies and future-ready digital 
infrastructure have materially strengthened connectivity 
across the country. 
The sector is at a pivotal stage of transformation, driven by 
rapid 5G adoption, rising data consumption and increasing 
demand for home broadband. In a short span of time, 5G 
coverage was rapidly expanded to 99.9% of the districts, 
on the back of high network investments. The expansion 
of 5G, along with deeper network availability in rural and 
underserved areas, has further reinforced the sector’s role 
in promoting economic progress and social inclusion. This 
is reflected in the growing adoption of digital payments, 
greater financial inclusion, and improved access to 
e-governance, healthcare, and education.
Digital network infrastructure has become a critical enabler 
of economic development, innovation and research. Through 
initiatives such as the AI Mission, National Quantum Mission, 
and the R&D and Innovation Fund, the Government is 
accelerating digital adoption. With the government focused 
on further improving digital penetration, Rajasthan and the 
North-East continue to emerge as structurally attractive 
growth markets, supported by significant headroom for tele-
density expansion.
Rajasthan is advancing its digital transformation through 
focused policy initiatives aimed at attracting investment 
in digital infrastructure, strengthening e-governance, and 
expanding connectivity. The State has implemented an 
integrated network architecture through the Rajasthan 
State-wide Area Network (RajSWAN), enabling last-mile 
connectivity down to Gram Panchayats and supporting 
seamless delivery of digital governance and public services, 
even in remote areas. Digital infrastructure development is 
also being supported by the Rajasthan Data Centre Policy 
2025, which seeks to position the State as a preferred 
destination for data centre investments through fiscal 
incentives, streamlined regulations, and sustainability-led 
measures. In parallel, the Rajasthan Global Capability Centre 
(GCC) Policy 2025 aims to attract global capability centres 
by leveraging the State’s skilled talent pool and robust digital 
infrastructure.
The Rajasthan AI/ ML Policy 2026, launched in January 
2026, underscores the State’s commitment to using 
advanced technologies to modernise public service delivery, 
improve transparency, foster innovation, and generate 
employment. To democratise access to the benefits of 
artificial intelligence, the State has also launched  
'SMART' - a system designed to build a Unified Ledger of 
schemes and entitlements by centralising data repositories, 
enabling automatic identification of beneficiaries and 
seamless delivery of benefits. These initiatives are 
expected to strengthen Rajasthan’s attractiveness as a 
digital investment destination, create jobs, and deepen its 
integration with the evolving services economy.
The North-East region is also undergoing a significant 
transformation, supported by sustained government focus 
under the Act East Policy and the Digital North-East Vision, 
including targeted investments of H500  billion under 
BharatNet. Events such as the North-East Investors Summit, 
which drew over H4.3 trillion of investment proposals with 
delegations from more than 80 countries, highlight the 
region’s emerging economic potential. Over the past decade, 
substantial investments exceeding H1.5 trillion have been 
made in digital and physical infrastructure. These efforts are 
improving connectivity in remote and border areas, driving 
greater digital inclusion, and integrating the region more 
closely with national and global economic networks. 
To capitalise on these growth opportunities, Bharti Hexacom 
continued to invest in building new digital infrastructure. 
In FY2025-26, the Company expanded its digital footprint 
with an investment of H15,210 million  to add 245 network 
towers and 3,657 mobile broadband base stations. 
Expansion of the home broadband business is being driven 
through an asset-light partnership model with local cable 
operators, while the rollout of Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) 
services across 267 cities during the year expanded the 
addressable market to areas with limited fiber presence. 
To augment its convergence strategy, Bharti Hexacom 
launched IPTV services across Rajasthan and the North-
East with encouraging response from customers. Backed 
by a strong brand, a comprehensive product portfolio and 
differentiated offerings, Bharti Hexacom is well positioned to 
sustain its growth momentum while further strengthening its 
market leadership.

Outlook
India’s economic outlook remains resilient, supported by 
robust domestic fundamentals and continued policy support. 
Real GDP growth is projected at 6.6% for FY 2026-273.
Domestic demand is expected to remain the primary driver 
of growth, shielding the economy to a significant extent 
from external shocks. Private consumption is likely to remain 
strong, supported by healthy macroeconomic fundamentals 
including stable inflation and improving income levels and 
steady urban consumption. Investment activity is expected 
to sustain momentum through continued government 
capital expenditure and a strong focus on infrastructure 
development.
Inflation is expected to rise to around 4.3% in FY2026-27, 
following a period of relatively low inflation in FY2025-26. 
Precious metal prices are expected to remain volatile. Risks 
persist from adverse weather conditions. Early forecasts 
from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) indicate 
that the 2026 southwest monsoon is likely to be below 
normal, with rainfall estimated at around 92% of the long- 
period average. A weaker monsoon may affect agricultural 
output and rural demand, while exerting inflationary 
pressure on food prices in the near term. 
On the external front, services exports are expected to 
retain their underlying strength, reinforcing India’s position 
in business and technology sectors globally. Ongoing trade 
agreements, including recent progress on India-Europe free 
trade arrangements, as the moderation of India-US tariffs, 
may provide incremental tailwinds to export growth over 
the medium term. However, global uncertainties may result 
in supply chain disruptions and financial market volatility, 
exerting pressure on external demand and capital flows. 
The Union Budget 2026-27 reaffirmed the government's 
commitment to infrastructure-led growth while sustaining 
fiscal consolidation. Public capital expenditure was raised to 
H12.2 trillion for FY2026-27, up from H11 trillion in FY2025-
26. Effective capital expenditure, including grants for capital 
asset creation, is projected at H17.1 trillion, equivalent to 
4.4% of GDP. 
The fiscal deficit target for FY2026-27 has been set at 
4.3% of GDP, continuing the consolidation trajectory. The 
Budget has significant implications for the digital and 
telecommunications sector.4
These developments, along with rising cross-border data 
flows, the expansion of Global Capability Centres and 
increasing digital adoption, are expected to support growth 
in technology-driven services and digital trade. India’s 
growing share in global services trade is estimated to reach 
around 10% by 2047, further strengthening its position as a 
services-driven and digitally integrated economy. Attracting 
FDI inflows remains important in a relatively subdued 
global investment environment to sustain India’s growth 
momentum.

Dominant Market Position: The Company currently 
stands  as a leading mobile operator, commanding a 
major share of revenue within its operational territories.
Global Brand Equity: Services are offered under the 
globally recognised "Airtel" brand.
Comprehensive Service Portfolio: It delivers mobile, 
fixed-line, high-speed Wi-Fi solutions (utilising both fibre-
to-the-home and fixed wireless access) and IPTV across 
Rajasthan and the North-East regions.
Synergistic B2C Convergence: The Company offers 
B2C services that bundle mobile with broadband and 
Digital TV. In collaboration with Bharti Airtel, it targets 
premium households through bundled offerings 
that deliver linear television channels and streaming 
applications alongside telecom services.
Future-Proof Network Infrastructure: Through steady 
expansion, the Company has built a vast digital network 
capable of handling rising demand for high-speed data. 
By leveraging data science and digital tools, Bharti 
Hexacom has reduced operational complexity and 
boosted overall efficiency.
Parent Company Synergies: The Company’s strategic 
relationship with Bharti Airtel Limited provides valuable 
operational advantages, including direct access to 
established digital infrastructure, and an experienced 
and capable leadership team.
Robust Financial Health: The Company maintains 
strong operating cash flows despite operating in a 
capital-intensive sector, ensuring a solid credit rating and 
a low-risk debt profile.
Procurement constraints: Shortages of critical 
network and non-network supplies may lead 
to delays in rollout plans. Global supply chain 
disruptions can further intensify these constraints, 
resulting in longer lead times and higher 
procurement costs. 
Pricing pressures: The telecom sector requires 
sustained, long-term capital investment, making 
an adequate and balanced tariff structure critical 
to maintaining industry viability and supporting 
continued investments in network expansion, 
technology upgrades, and service quality.
5G Monetisation: Despite significant investments 
in spectrum and network infrastructure, 
monetising 5G remains a challenge due to limited 
availability of differentiated consumer use cases. 
At present, 5G access is offered at no additional 
charge to postpaid customers and eligible prepaid 
users on select unlimited plans, limiting the pace of 
capital recovery.

Context
Telecom networks are exposed to risks from technical 
failures, partner dependencies, human errors, wilful acts 
and natural disasters. Factors such as equipment delays or 
failures, spare shortages, energy or fuel shortages, software 
errors, fiber cuts, inadequate redundancy paths, weak 
disaster recovery mechanisms and partner unavailability 
can adversely impact network availability and service 
continuity.
Impact
The Company’s IT systems are critical to its customer 
and market-facing operations and in running its internal 
systems. In some geographies, the last mile IT connectivity 
can sometimes be erratic or unreliable, affecting service 
delivery. The quality of IT staff and the ever-changing 
systems landscape also add risk to the quality and 
continuity of service. Also, the systems landscape is rapidly 
evolving with newer versions, upgrades and ‘patches’ for 
innovations and price changes, among others.
Mitigating Actions
The Company operates advanced Network Operations 
Centers (NOCs) to monitor network performance in 
real time and ensure high network availability. Network 
planning is increasingly managed in-house to strengthen 
architectural control and improve long-term reliability. 
The Company continuously enhances network quality 
by addressing congestion, improving indoor coverage, 
reducing call drops, increasing data speeds, and 
resolving other network issues through structured quality 
improvement programmes. Network performance is 
regularly measured against network stability, customer 
experience, and industry benchmarks.
The Company continues to eliminate single points of 
failure (SPOFs) across its core network, transmission 
infrastructure, and critical fiber routes. Redundancy 
measures are built into key network components to 
minimise the impact of power outages, fiber cuts, VSAT 
failures, and other disruptions. Critical network elements are 
deployed on resilient transport architecture with multiple 
backup paths to ensure service continuity.
Disaster Recovery Plans (DRPs), Network Recovery 
Plans (NRPs), and Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) are 
established across all operating circles to enable timely 
recovery from unforeseen events. Network infrastructure 
is strengthened through geographic redundancy, diverse 
fiber routes, and resilient tower designs in disaster-prone 
regions.
The resilience of its IT infrastructure is continually 
strengthened through regular assessment of hardware, 
software, and system architecture to ensure reliable and 
uninterrupted business operations.
Operational resilience is enhanced through infrastructure-
sharing partnerships and increased automation of 
network operations, improving efficiency while reducing 
manual intervention.

Gaps in prevention of Data 
Loss (Operational)
Outlook from last year: Stable
Context
Personal data refers to any information about an individual, 
that can be used to identify them. In an increasingly digital 
environment where large volumes of personal data are 
shared globally, maintaining control over such information 
is challenging. Data protection refers to the practices and 
safeguards put in place to protect personal information, that 
ensure an individual can decide if, how and with whom they 
share their information, who has access to it, for how long 
and for what purpose, while retaining the right to modify 
and control the flow of this information. Data protection 
must strike a balance between the use of personal data for 
business purposes and ensuring compliance with applicable 
data privacy regulations.
Impact
Data privacy regulations were put in place by several 
countries, most notably the European Union, which passed 
the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in 2018. 
India also passed the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 
in August 2023. The Company has initiated its efforts to 
ensure compliance with the legislation. 
Mitigating Actions
The Company’s privacy policy ensures that personal data 
collected by the Company is processed, retained, shared 
and disposed of in accordance with the applicable data 
privacy regulations and contractual obligations. The Data 
Loss Prevention (DLP) strategy at the Company has been 
designed to protect information at their most vulnerable 
points, i.e. at the endpoint, at the web layer and at the email 
layer.
All endpoints are equipped with specialised DLP software, 
which helps to monitor potential data leakage across 
various channels, triggering alerts to enable timely review 
and investigation of potential incidents. Similar solutions are 
deployed at the email and web gateway. Alerts are centrally 
monitored and incidents are tracked to ensure closure within 
defined timelines, with monthly reviews used to strengthen 
data security policies. Additionally, the organisation has 
invested in specialised software to detect sensitive data in 
APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) to ensure similar 
levels of security for all machine-to-machine communication 
as exists for all human-to-machine communication. The 
Company continues to explore and adopt new technologies 
to further enhance data security.
Capitals Impacted
Material issues for The Company
•	 Information security and customer data privacy.

Lack of Digitisation and 
Innovations (Strategic)
Outlook from last year: Emerging
Context
The telecom sector continues to undergo rapid and 
accelerating digital transformation, with technology 
increasingly determining competitive position. The same 
forces that create opportunity also lower barriers to entry: 
Generative AI, agentic systems, and real-time inference at 
scale allow OTT players, hyperscalers, and digital-native 
challengers to capture value that has historically sat adjacent 
to the network. An operator that remains a connectivity 
provider risks commoditization to a transport-only role, with 
value and the primary customer relationship migrating up 
the stack to those who own the digital experience. The risk is 
structural and time-sensitive: organizations slow to convert 
experimentation into large-scale deployment cede relevance, 
margin, and differentiation that are difficult to recover once 
lost.
Impact
If the pace of digitisation and innovation lags the pace of 
market change, the Company will get exposed on 5 fronts:
•	 Customer relevance and differentiation erode, increasing 
churn toward more digital-native competitors.
•	 Revenue concentrates in commoditised connectivity, 
compressing ARPU and margins as value migrates to the 
application and platform layers.
•	 High-growth enterprise demand for cloud, edge, and 
sovereign infrastructure is captured by hyperscalers and 
specialised providers.
•	 Operating costs remain structurally higher in the absence 
of digital and AI-led efficiency compared to peers.
•	 Slow conversion from pilot to scale turns an early-mover 
advantage into a late-follower disadvantage, particularly 
in agentic AI and real-time inference.
Mitigating actions
Digitisation and innovation remain foundational strategic 
priorities for the Company. During FY 2025-26, the Company 
has accelerated its digital transformation agenda across 
three interconnected fronts: customer-facing innovation, 
platform monetisation, and core business digitalisation that 
reflect a comprehensive, enterprise-wide commitment to 
competitive differentiation.
The Company's digital strategy continues to be 
anchored on three pillars:
•	 Launch of new products with a digital-first approach, 
ensuring a consistent and seamless experience across 
touchpoints; now augmented by AI-native product design.
•	 Simplification of the customer lifecycle through self-
service and omni-channel capabilities, increasingly 
powered by agentic AI.
•	 Making the core of business digital to drive both 
experience excellence and operational efficiency, enabled 
through the Xtelify platform ecosystem.

Climate Change and Energy 
Management (Strategic)
Outlook from last year: Emerging
Context
Natural disasters have severely impacted livelihoods and 
infrastructure, including telecommunication infrastructure. 
Telecommunication plays a pivotal role at each stage of 
disaster management, from early warning and mitigation 
to response, extending to post-disaster recovery and 
rehabilitation.
Impact
Climate-related risks may degrade telecom infrastructure, 
adversely affect service availability and quality, increase 
business costs, impact maintenance and repair operations 
and pose health and safety risks to personnel.
Mitigating Actions
The Company has devised a climate-resilience plan to build 
and re-engineer its telecom infrastructure:
Flood-prone areas design criteria 
•	 Adopt lean tower designs with elevated platform 
foundations (EPF) and relocate passive infrastructure to 
raised platforms in areas prone to heavy flooding. 
•	 Installation of equipment preferably at elevated areas. 
•	 Maintain higher plinth levels. 
•	 Ensure ToCo partners build site based on historical flood 
data and Central Water Commission (CWC) reports and 
maintain appropriate plinth height. 
•	 Develop secure, elevated access pathways to passive 
infrastructure. 
•	 Relocate active infrastructure above recorded flood levels. 
•	 Use flood-resistant building materials; implement swales 
and efficient drainage systems. 
•	 Deploy early flood warning systems.
•	 Retrofit critical infrastructure or assets vulnerable to 
flooding (e.g. electrical equipment).
Water scarce areas design criteria: 
•	 Put in place blue roofs, rainwater harvesting and reuse, 
greywater recycling and wastewater heat recovery 
systems.
•	 Install water efficient fixtures and appliances, implement 
leak detection systems and conduct regular inspections. 
Cyclone- and wind-prone areas design criteria:
•	 Consider factor of safety (as per IS codes) while designing 
telecom infrastructure.
•	 Remove Cells on Wheels (CoW), microwave and unsafe 
towers, build permanent structures.
•	 Install RRUs behind base station antenna to reduce wind 
exposure area.
•	 Avoid microwave dishes of >1.2m diameter. Install 
microwave with supporting rod to avoid misalignment. 
•	 Install V clamp instead of U clamp for improved grip. 
•	 Undertake tower loading in terms of antennas and other 
equipment loads as per design document. 
•	 Design the base for roof top tower (RTT) adequately in 
order to transfer the tower load onto the building’s RCC 
grid. Obtain a structural safety certificate from a qualified 
structural engineer.
•	 Design towers as per provisions of the latest B.I.S. codes 
of practice governing design. 
•	 Carry out regular preventive maintenance and structural 
health assessments of infrastructure.
Temperature-related design criteria 
•	 Put in place white roofs or use light/ highly reflective 
colours to bounce back solar radiation and reduce heat 
absorption.
•	 Incorporate green roofs and vegetation to improve 
building’s insulation and aid heat dissipation.
•	 Improve glazing performance and install blinds/ fixed 
external shading devices.
•	 Use heat-resistant materials.
Capitals Impacted
Material Issues for the Company
•	 Climate change, energy efficiency and emission reduction. 
•	 Sustainable supply chain management.

a.	
Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/No). 
If yes, the coverage of such system? Yes. Bharti Hexacom has implemented a comprehensive Occupational Health 
and Safety Management System (OHSMS) and it is ISO 45001 certified. The OHSMS covers the Company’s offices, 
network operations, and field activities. Safety governance is driven through the overarching “Airtel Suraksha” 
programme, supported by central and circle-level safety committees, and reinforced through policies and SOPs 
including the Workplace Safety Policy, Infrastructure Safety Policy, Supplier Safety Policy, Women Safety Policy, 
travel safety guidelines.
	
The Company has implemented robust OHSMS awareness initiatives through regular training programs, safety 
communications, emailers, newsletters, a dedicated safety microsite, competitions, workshops, and other employee 
engagement activities to promote awareness and strengthen the safety culture.
b.	
What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine 
basis by the entity? Bharti Hexacom identifies work-related hazards and assesses risks for routine and non-routine 
activities through a structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process. Key processes include:
•	
Health and safety audit (including periodic reviews of the OHSMS) to identify gaps and define control-focused 
action plans
•	
Health and safety performance review through management review of predefined safety KPIs, incident 
trends, audit findings and progress on safety goals
•	
Incident investigation and risk analysis wherein all reported incidents are investigated from both policy 
compliance and risk assessment perspectives. Detailed root cause analysis is conducted to identify underlying 
causes, assess severity and potential impacts and define effective corrective and preventive actions. Where 
required, investigations include on-ground verification and site visits by safety teams to ensure thorough 
analysis and effective closure
•	
Proactive Reporting of Unsafe Acts and Conditions by employees and associates to enable early identification 
of hazards, timely risk mitigation and prevention of incidents

such risks. (Yes/No):
	
	
Yes. Bharti Hexacom has established multiple channels for workers to report work-related hazards, near-misses, 
and safety violations, such as a toll-free number printed on ID cards, central/local email channels, and an incident 
reporting application “Airtel Shield”. Workers are also empowered to stop work and remove themselves from unsafe 
situations (“stop-work authority”) without fear of retaliation, and work is resumed only after the hazard is assessed 
and appropriate controls are implemented and verified by the respective safety teams.

Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words/web-link: 
Yes, Airtel has established the “Bharti Information Security Policy” version 9.0, which is aligned and compliant with 
ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 22301:2019. This policy, as referenced in section 14.4.1 on BCMS plan documentation 
and implementation, defines a structured methodology for documenting and implementing the BCMS Manual and 
associated plans, which are prepared and maintained by units across circles and central functions. Airtel performs 
periodic BIAs to identify critical processes and dependencies and define RTOs, RPOs, and recovery priorities aligned 
to business and regulatory impact. 
	
BCMS documents undergo periodic review and are validated through annual testing to ensure their effectiveness in 
meeting defined recovery objectives. The Company also maintains ISO 22301:2019 certification for the circle offices of 
Bharti Hexacom, MSCs, network warehouses, and operational sites, in accordance with regulatory requirements issued 
by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). Comprehensive business continuity plans have been developed 
to ensure uninterrupted continuity of critical operations, including provisions for alternate site working and remote 
access, supported by appropriate infrastructure, technology and qualified workforce. Formal guidelines have been 
communicated to relevant stakeholders, covering disaster preparedness elements such as risk assessment, resource 
planning, incident response, and recovery procedures. 
	
The Company conducts periodic tabletop exercises, disaster recovery (DR) drills for applications, and end-to-end 
process recovery tests to assess overall resilience and readiness. A centralized Network Operations Centre (NOC) 
provides real-time monitoring of network activities, and this is complemented by a robust insurance framework to 
protect organizational assets against risks such as fire and natural disasters.

additional/ upgraded battery banks resulting in saving

infrastructure partners, we are transforming our sites 
into eco-friendly ones. 75% of our network sites, 
including both owned by Hexacom as well as by 
partners, have been tagged as green sites, consuming 
less than 100 litres of diesel per quarter.

infrastructure, our site sharing strategy with partners 
has optimised our resource usage.

and Machine Learning algorithms are implemented 
to put to sleep radios of less load so that other cells 
can take the traffic. This has resulted in the saving of

high footfall areas and peak traffic duration

Scale AirFiber (FWA) on SA:  Bharti Hexacom 
has migrated Fixed Wireless Access (FWA)

aimed to deliver a better and more consistent 
user experience for FWA devices, particularly 
in uplink-heavy use cases, by leveraging the SA 
and 5G Advance capability and  at the same time

farmed to 5G in select areas in order to extend

efficient way of deploying 5G by reusing existing

only accelerates 5G footprint expansion but also 
enhances indoor 5G coverage, enabling higher 
time spent on 5G. The initiative will be expanded 
to additional cities to further strengthen Airtel’s 5G

address this, Radio Network enhancement done 
on top of existing mitigations capabilities that 
improves uplink stability, boosts uplink throughput

Report on Corporate Governance
This Corporate Governance Report outlines Bharti Hexacom Limited’s (‘Bharti Hexacom’/ ‘Hexacom’/ ‘the Company’) 
commitment to adopting and strengthening best-in-class Corporate Governance practices. It reflects upon the ethical 
business standards followed by Bharti Hexacom, in tandem with a robust governance framework reinforced by the policies 
and procedures to ensure transparency, accountability, and integrity in all its operations. These measures are aimed at 
fostering responsible business conduct and enabling sustainable, long-term value creation for all stakeholders.
Corporate Governance Philosophy
Our Corporate Governance philosophy is anchored in our core values, which guide our conduct everyday i.e. (i) Trust, 
transparency and integrity; (ii) Deep and fair relationship with our stakeholders; and (iii) Ethical business practices and 
standards. We believe that Corporate Governance is a means to achieve the Company’s vision and objectives, in a transparent, 
ethical and legally compliant manner, while ensuring the best interests of all the stakeholders.

MOA and AOA: The Company’s operations are carried 
out in accordance with the objects and powers specified 
in its Memorandum of Association (‘MOA’). The Articles 
of Association (‘AOA’) provide a robust governance 
framework by delineating the respective powers, rights, and 
responsibilities of the Board of Directors and Shareholders. 
It also sets out the procedures to ensure the orderly, 
transparent, and compliant management of the Company’s 
affairs.
Shareholders: Shareholders are the capital contributors 
who have bestowed their trust in the Company’s business 
objectives, the Board and the management. As the ultimate 
owners of the Company they exercise their rights through key 
decisions. Pursuant to the Companies Act, 2013 (‘the Act’), 
the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing Regulations’), and other 
applicable laws, shareholder approval is sought for material 
matters, including fund raising, approval of financial 
statements, appointment and remuneration of Directors, 
appointment of statutory auditors, etc. Such approvals are 
obtained at the Annual General Meeting, Extra-Ordinary 
General Meeting, or through Postal Ballot, as and when 
required.
Board of Directors: The Board of Directors are the trustees 
entrusted with strategic oversight and the supervision of 
business operations, the management’s performance and 
governance of the Company on behalf of shareholders 
and other stakeholders. The Board exercises independent 
judgment and plays a pivotal role in monitoring the 
Company’s overall affairs and ensures that the business is 
conducted sustainably and aligned with the MOA and AOA 
of the Company and all the applicable laws. The Board is 
headed by a Non-executive Chairman, who ensures an 
effective and robust Board culture. A brief profile of all the 
Directors, nature of their expertise in specific functional 
areas, etc. are available on the website of the Company 
which can be accessed by clicking here and is also provided 
separately in this Annual Report.
Board Committees: The Board Committees are specialised 
bodies constituted to enhance the effectiveness of the 
Board by objectively examining complex agenda items 
and providing well-considered recommendations. These 
Committees enable focused deliberations and facilitate 
the timely and efficient resolution of diverse matters. The 
Chairman of each Committee presents a summary of the 
discussions, decisions and recommendations at the ensuing 
meeting of the Board of Directors. This enables them to 
devote greater attention to strategic matters and utilise its 
time and efforts more efficiently, while continuing to retain 
collective responsibility for all decisions.
Senior Management: Senior Management is the executive 
body which closely implements the approved strategies 
under the guidance of the Board and its Committees. They 
also ensure smooth management of the Company focusing 
on compliance, financial and operational performance and 
sustainability. Depending on the roles, the key performance 
indicators of Senior Management generally include financials 
viz. growth, margin, EBITDA, working capital and revenue, etc. 
and non-financial parameters cover compliance, stakeholder 
management, digitisation, talent management, diversity and 
sustainability/ ESG, etc. The profile of Senior Management 
is available on the website of the Company which can be 
accessed by clicking here.
Company Secretary and Compliance Officer: The Company 
Secretary and Compliance Officer steers Board excellence 
and compliance by building robust governance models. 
Through structured policies and open feedback channels, 
they deliver critical guidance and bridge communication 
across all stakeholders.
The roles and responsibilities of Company Secretary include 
(i) adherence to the Board processes and procedures; 
(ii) convening the Board, Committee and General Meetings 
of the Company and ensuring availability of relevant 
information for effective decision making; (iii) ensuring 
action points arising from the Board/  Committee meetings 
are communicated to the Management and an update is 
provided to the Board/  Committees; (iv) assist the Board/ 
Committees in developing policies and processes around 
applicable laws viz. related party transactions, Board 
evaluation, Board familiarisation, Board/ Committee role 
and responsibilities, remuneration, loans and advances, 
investments, succession planning, compliance of applicable 
laws  and other environmental, social and governance 
matters (‘ESG’), etc. for ensuring strict adherence to law 
in letter and spirit; and (v) act as an interface between the 
Board, management and stakeholders. 
Auditors: The Statutory Auditors, Secretarial Auditors and 
Cost Auditors act as an organisational shield who carry out 
an independent, fair and transparent assessment of the 
financial statements, policies, practices and compliances 
of corporate law by the Company which strengthens the 
stakeholder confidence. All the Auditors have direct access 
to the Chairman of the Audit Committee for reporting any 
observations or concerns to ensure complete independence 
throughout the Audit process.
Internal Auditor (IA) and Internal Assurance Partners: 
The Internal Auditor continuously assesses the adequacy 
and effectiveness of the Company’s internal controls by 
evaluating potential operational, business, financial and 
legal risks, thereby acting as safeguard against such risks.

The Audit Committee (‘Committee’) is pleased to 
present its report for the year ended March 31, 2026:
1.	
As on March 31, 2026, the Committee comprised five 
members, of whom four including the Chairman, are 
Independent Directors, in compliance with the requirement 
of at least two-thirds Independent Directors as prescribed 
under Regulation 18 of the Securities and Exchange Board 
of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 and Section 177 of the Companies 
Act, 2013. During the year under review, the Committee 
met six times and the attendance of the members was in 
compliance with the regulatory requirements. The Chief 
Financial Officer and the Company Secretary attend 
the meetings of the Committee as permanent invitees. 
In addition, members of the Senior Management are 
invited to attend the meetings, as and when required, 
by the Chairman of the Committee to facilitate informed 
deliberations and provide inputs on matters within their 
respective areas of responsibility.
2.	
The responsibility for the Company’s internal controls and 
financial reporting processes lies with the Management. The 
Statutory Auditors have the responsibility of performing an 
independent audit of the Company’s financial statements 
in accordance with the Indian Accounting Standards (Ind-
AS) and issuing a report thereon. The Ombudsperson is 
responsible for the Company’s Whistle Blower Mechanism.
3.	
The Company has in place an Internal Assurance Group 
(IAG) led by Puneet Diwan. He is the Internal Auditor in 
accordance with Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013. 
The Company had also appointed Ernst & Young LLP and 
ANB & Co., Chartered Accountants, Mumbai as the Internal 
Assurance Partners. The audit conducted by the Internal 
Auditors and Internal Assurance Partners is based on an 
internal audit plan, reviewed annually in consultation with 
the IAG and the Audit Committee. These audits are based on 
a risk-based methodology and interalia involve the review of 
internal controls and governance processes, adherence to 
management policies and review of statutory compliances. 
The Internal Assurance Partners share their findings on an 
ongoing basis during the year for corrective action.
4.	
The Audit Committee oversees the work of the Statutory 
Auditors, Internal Auditor, Internal Assurance Partners and 
the Ombudsperson. It is also responsible for overseeing 
processes relating to the financial reporting and 
information dissemination.
Audit Committee Report for financial year 2025-26
5.	
In this regard, the Audit Committee reports as follows:
	
I.	
The Committee has discussed with the Company’s 
Internal Auditors, Internal Assurance Partners and 
Statutory Auditors the overall scope and plan for 
their respective audits. The Committee has also 
discussed the results and effectiveness of the audit, 
evaluation of the Company’s internal controls and the 
overall quality of financial reporting. The Committee 
also met the Statutory Auditors without the presence 
of Management, ensuring independent and open 
discussion.
	
II.	
The Management has presented the Company’s 
financial statements to the Committee and affirmed 
that the Company’s financial statements have been 
drawn in accordance with Ind-AS. Based on its review 
and the discussions held with the Management and 
the Statutory Auditors, the Committee believes that 
the Company’s financial statements are presented 
fairly  in material aspects, in conformity with 
applicable accounting standards. The Committee 
also considers that the financial statements are 
true and fair and provide sufficient information. The 
Committee believes that the Company has followed 
adequate processes to prepare these financial 
statements.
	
III.	
The Committee has reviewed the standalone financial 
statements for the year ended March 31, 2026. It has 
recommended the same for the Board’s approval.
	
IV.	
The Committee has reviewed the internal controls 
to ensure that the Company’s accounts are properly 
maintained and that the accounting transactions are 
in accordance with prevailing laws and regulations. In 
conducting such reviews, the Committee found that 
the Company’s internal control systems are overall 
designed adequately and are operating satisfactorily. 
Where deficiencies or improvement areas  are pointed 
out by  internal audit, the Management has taken 
adequate steps or is in process of addressing those 
areas.
	
V.	
The Committee reviewed the Company’s internal 
financial controls and risk management systems on 
a ongoing basis.
	
VI.	
The Committee reviewed the Ombudsperson’s 
report on the functioning of the Whistle Blower 
Mechanism for reporting concerns about unethical 
behaviour, actual or suspected fraud, or violation 
of the Company’s Code of Conduct or ethics policy. 
The Committee believes that the Company has an 
effective Whistle Blower Mechanism and that nobody 
has been denied access to this mechanism.
	
VII.	 The Committee has reviewed, with  Management, 
the independence, effectiveness of Audit process 
and performance of Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP, 
Chartered Accountants, being the Statutory Auditors 
of the Company.
	
VIII.	 The Committee, along with the Management, 
reviewed the performance of the Internal Assurance 
Partners viz. Ernst & Young LLP and ANB & Co., 
Chartered Accountants, Mumbai and also reviewed 
the adequacy of internal control systems. The 
Committee has also reviewed the eligibility and 
independence of Ernst & Young LLP and ANB & 
Co. and has recommended to the Board the re-
appointment of Ernst & Young LLP and ANB & Co. as 
internal assurance partners. 
	
IX.	
The Committee has been vested with  adequate 
powers to seek support and other resources from 
the Company. The Committee has access to the 
information and records. It also has the authority to 
obtain professional advice from external sources, if 
required.
	
X.	
The Committee reviewed and approved all related 
party transactions, including any modifications or 
amendments thereto. All such transactions were 
found to be in the ordinary course of business and 
conducted on an arm’s length basis.
	
XI.	
The Committee has reviewed the systems and 
processes in line with requirements of the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015 and Company’s Code of 
Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading.
	
XII.	 The Audit Committee oversaw a comprehensive 
and transparent process for the selection of 
the Company’s successor Statutory Auditors, in 
view of the completion of Deloitte’s maximum 
permissible tenure at the conclusion of the 32nd 
Annual General Meeting scheduled in 2027. After an 
extensive evaluation of eligible audit firms, including 
assessment of their credentials, industry expertise, 
audit quality framework, independence and capability 
to serve an organization of the Company’s scale and 
complexity, the Audit Committee recommended 
the appointment of S.R. Batliboi & Associates LLP, 
Chartered Accountants as the Statutory Auditors 
of the Company. Based on the Committee’s 
recommendation, the Board approved the proposed 
appointment, subject to the approval of the 
shareholders, with effect from the conclusion of the 
32nd Annual General Meeting.
In conclusion, the Audit Committee confirms that it has 
effectively discharged its responsibilities in accordance with 
its Charter, applicable laws, and regulatory requirements. The 
Committee is satisfied with the robustness of the Company’s 
governance, risk management, and internal control systems.

CODES, POLICIES AND FRAMEWORKS
Code of Conduct
The Company’s Code of Conduct (‘Code’) sets out the 
fundamental principles and standards that guide ethical, 
transparent, and responsible business conduct. The Code 
reflects the Company’s commitment to compliance with 
applicable laws and regulations, fostering a safe, inclusive, and 
harassment-free workplace, preventing conflict of interest, 
promoting fairness and mutual respect in all interactions, 
maintaining the highest standards of integrity, and upholding 
a zero-tolerance approach towards bribery, corruption, and 
other unethical practices, while safeguarding the Company’s 
reputation and values.
The Code applies to all the Directors, Senior Management, 
and employees of the Company. Annual affirmations of 
compliance with the Code are obtained. In addition, Senior 
Management provides quarterly confirmation of material 
financial and commercial transactions with the Company 
that may give rise to potential conflict of interest. A 
consolidated report of such disclosures is submitted to the 
Audit Committee and Board on quarterly basis. Based on 
the confirmations received during the year, no instance of 
conflict of interest was reported in the financial year 2025-
26. The code is available on the website of the Company 
which can be accessed by clicking here.
Regular training programs are conducted across locations 
to explain and reiterate the importance of adherence to the 
Code. 
Periodic internal audits are conducted to ensure effectiveness 
of the compliance with the Code and a report is presented 
to the Audit Committee as per the internal audit process 
and plan.
A declaration signed by the CEO, regarding affirmation of the 
compliance with the Code by the Board Members and Senior 
Management for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, 
is annexed as Annexure A to this Corporate Governance 
report.
The Company has adopted a Group-level Code of Conduct 
for Business Associates (‘COC-BA’), applicable to all 
suppliers, contractors, service providers, and other business 
associates. The COC-BA requires adherence to the highest 
standards of integrity, ethical conduct, and compliance, 
and prohibits all forms of bribery, corruption, and other 
unethical practices. It also mandates the monitoring and 
reporting of ESG practices in line with its requirements of 
the Code. The Company has established a framework to 
select and evaluate Business Associates against these 
standards and where necessary, undertake appropriate 
corrective measures, including training, capacity building, 
or termination of engagement based on the intensity of 
observation. The COC-BA is available at the website of the 
Company which can be accessed by clicking here.
The Company has instituted a comprehensive Vigil 
Mechanism as an integral component of its Code of 
Conduct. The mechanism serves as a secure, confidential, 
and accessible channel through which the employees 
and other stakeholders may report concerns relating to 
unethical behaviour, actual or suspected fraud, breaches 
of applicable laws, regulations, or the Code, and other 
instances of misconduct. Designed to foster a culture of 
integrity and accountability, the Vigil Mechanism enables 
individuals to raise genuine concerns without fear of 
retaliation, victimisation, or any adverse repercussions, and 
also facilitates anonymous reporting. It incorporates a well-
defined framework governing the reporting, investigation, and 
resolution of complaints, while ensuring strict confidentiality 
and appropriate safeguards for whistle blower. The Audit 
Committee oversees and reviews on a quarterly basis, the 
effectiveness and functioning of the Vigil Mechanism.
Administered by independent office of an Ombudsperson 
at group level, the entire formal process of reviewing and 
investigating the concerns raised, undertaking appropriate 
actions for resolution thereof and regular monitoring of 
process is ensured seamlessly with utmost confidentiality. All 
employees of the Company (full-time or part-time) as well as 
the external stakeholders (e.g. associate, strategic partners, 
vendors, suppliers, contractors, customers, etc.) have full 
access to the Ombudsperson through secure hotline, Email 
(ombudsperson@bharti.in), post (Ombudsperson Office 
Bharti Hexacom Limited, Bharti Crescent, 1, Nelson Mandela 
Road, Vasant Kunj, Phase II, New Delhi-110070, India) or even 
meeting in person. The stakeholders also have the unfettered 
right to escalate the complaints to the Audit Committee 
Chairman in special cases through a dedicated Email id. Also, 
no person was denied access to the Audit Committee.

The Company has instituted a robust Code of Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading (‘Code’) in strict compliance with the 
SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (‘Insider Trading Regulations’) to regulate, monitor and govern trading 
activities by Designated Persons (DPs) and their immediate relatives. During the period under review, the Code was proactively 
and dynamically amended to ensure continued alignment with evolving regulatory requirements under the Insider Trading 
Regulations.
Mandatory Pre-clearance: 
All trades undertaken by DPs or 
their Immediate relatives require 
prior approval, irrespective of value 
or volume.
Trading Volume Cap: 
Quarterly liquidations by DPs are 
restricted at 25% of their total 
holding or 50,000 equity shares, 
whichever is higher.
The Code lays down comprehensive procedures governing trading in the Company’s securities, including shares and 
derivatives. It clearly delineates the roles, responsibilities and obligations of DPs, inter alia, maintenance of the Structured 
Digital Database (SDD), protocols for the prevention of insider trading mechanisms and handling Unpublished Price Sensitive 
Information (UPSI), and processes to promote confidentiality and data integrity. It also specifies prohibited trades and 
establishes a structured framework for execution of permissible transactions.
Demonstrating a strong commitment to the highest standards of Corporate Governance, the Company adopted a compliance 
regime that goes beyond statutory mandates, in adherence with the Insider Trading Regulations in both letter and spirit. 
Key voluntary measures include:
Digital Platform for Disclosures:
During the year, the Company has deployed a secure, web-based automated platform enabling DPs to submit disclosures 
and obtain pre-clearance for proposed trades. This system enhances efficiency, transparency, and accuracy in compliance 
reporting.

is placed before the Audit Committee on a half-yearly basis.
The Company has institutionalised a structured training and 
awareness framework. It periodically circulates compliance 
updates, compliance FAQs, and ‘Do’s and Don’ts’ to 
Designated Persons. This is supplemented by frequent 
interactive workshops and targeted training sessions to 
continuously educate and sensitise personnel. To ensure 
absolute control over the dissemination of UPSI during 
the discharge of official duties, the Company operates 
an advanced, web-based automated Structured Digital 
Database (SDD) tool.
Additionally, the Company has also formulated a Code of 
Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of UPSI as per 
the requirements of the Insider Trading Regulations which 
is available on the website of the Company and can be 
accessed by clicking here. 
As a part of digital transformation and data integrity, 
we introduced a digital platform for disclosure by all 
Designated Persons under the PIT Code. This initiative 
streamlines compliance and enhances the accuracy of 
reporting through a secure and automated platform.
The Company has formulated a comprehensive Board 
approved Policy on Related Party Transactions (‘RPT Policy’) 
that sets out the governing framework for determining 
materiality thresholds and regulating process for all related 
party arrangements, pursuant to the applicable provisions 
of the Act and the SEBI Listing Regulations. All identified 
Related Party Transactions (RPTs), including any subsequent 
material modifications, are reviewed and approved by the 
Audit Committee in strict compliance with the statutory 
mandates. To ensure adherence to arm’s length principles, 
such transactions are undertaken only after comprehensive 
review and certification by leading independent, global 
valuation and accounting firms.
The RPT Policy mandates that any member of the Audit 
Committee with a potential interest in a proposed transaction 
must recuse themselves and abstain from all deliberations 
and voting on the matter. The RPT policy can be accessed 
by clicking here.
The Company has adopted a comprehensive format for 
approval of Related Party Transactions in strict accordance 
with the SEBI circular on Industry Standards on Minimum 
Information (ISN) to be provided to the Audit Committee 
and shareholders for such RPTs. The approval notes are 
structured to capture all prescribed minimum information, 
including nature of relationship, transaction details, value 
and tenure, arm’s length and ordinary course assessment, 
pricing/ benchmarking, materiality thresholds and purpose 
and commercial rationale, along with identification of 
material modifications and omnibus approval parameters, 
wherever applicable. Further, each proposal is supported by 
a CEO and CFO certification confirming that the proposed 
transactions are in the best interest of the Company. Thus, 
this approach with the SEBI-prescribed ISN framework 
ensures completeness, consistency and transparency of 
information, thereby enabling informed decision-making 
and robust governance.
Digitisation of RPT framework
The Company has implemented a robust digital RPT 
management tool for monitoring and tracking transactions 
with related parties, to enhance governance, compliance 
and oversight processes. The tool enables centralised 
master data management of related parties, automated 
flagging of potential RPTs through system integrations and 
end-to-end workflow-based approvals aligned with the RPT 
Policy. It also facilitates real-time tracking of transaction 
values against approved limits, identification of material 
modifications and generation of audit-ready reports for 
regulatory disclosures and internal reviews. The system 
strengthens governance by ensuring proactive compliance, 
enhanced traceability and minimised risk of oversight, while 
providing stakeholders with a transparent and efficient 
mechanism for managing RPTs.
Related Party Transactions 
Our robust Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework 
developed at group level enables us to facilitate enterprise-
wide identification, assessment, and mitigation of key 
risks through well-defined response plans ensuring that 
the Company is able to manage and align its strategies to 
identified risk and stay ahead of the curve. 
A detailed update on the risk governance structure, key 
elements of the framework, and mitigation of strategic risks 
is provided in the ‘Risk and Mitigation Framework’ section 
forming part of this Annual Report.
In line with the requirements of Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations, the Company has developed a comprehensive 
policy for Determining Materiality of Events /  Information. The 
Policy inter-alia provides for the quantitative and qualitative 
criteria for determining material event/  information including 
deemed material information, and timelines within which the 
information should be disclosed to the Stock  Exchanges i.e., 
BSE and NSE. 
All transactions entered into by the Company with its related parties during the financial year ended March 31, 2026, were 
executed in the ordinary course of business and on an arm’s length basis, thereby falling outside the restrictive purview of 
Section 188 of the Act. Prior approvals from the Audit Committee and, wherever applicable, the Shareholders were duly 
obtained wherever mandated under the SEBI Listing Regulations.
During the financial year 2025-26, the Company did not enter into any materially significant related party transactions 
that could pose a potential conflict of interest or is prejudicial to the interests of the Company or its minority shareholders.

Summary of material accounting policies
2.1	 Basis of preparation
	
These Financial Statements have been prepared 
to comply in all material respects with the Indian 
Accounting Standards (‘Ind AS’) as notified by the 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (‘MCA’) under section 133 
of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’), read together with 
Rule 3 of the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) 
Rules, 2015 (as amended from time to time) and other 
accounting principles generally accepted in India.
	
The Financial Statements are approved for issue by the 
Company’s Board of Directors on May 13, 2026, held in 
Gurugram.
	
The Financial Statements are based on the classification 
provisions contained in Ind AS 1, ‘Presentation of 
Financial Statements’ and division II of schedule III (as 
amended) to the Act. Further, for the purpose of clarity, 
various items are aggregated in the Balance Sheet, 
Statement of Profit and Loss, Statement of Changes 
in Equity, Statement of Cash Flows and accompanying 
notes. Nonetheless, these items are dis-aggregated 
separately in the notes to the Financial Statements, 
where applicable or required.
	
All the amounts included in the Financial Statements 
are reported in millions of Indian Rupee (‘Rupee’ or 
‘H’) and are rounded to the nearest million, except per 
share data and unless stated otherwise. Further, due to 
rounding off, certain amounts are appearing as ‘0’.
	
The preparation of the said Financial Statements 
requires the use of certain critical accounting estimates 
and judgements. It also requires the management to 
exercise judgement in the process of applying the 
Company’s accounting policies. The areas where 
estimates are significant to the Financial Statements, 
or areas involving a higher degree of judgement or
